extracted.subtask_description: Produce a short newswire-style press release announcing organizational news (newsletter launch) including headline, dateline, lead, body details, boilerplate, and contact information. Suitable for distribution on newswire services and to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise, descriptive title that summarizes the main news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page's headline is 'Third edition of the international newsletter from Aberje reflects on the country's crisis' — it states what (third edition of newsletter) and a hook (reflects on the country's crisis). Use a clear, informative single-line headline to attract attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and newswire marker
rubrics_metrics.description: A dateline providing city and date, often followed by a newswire identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example on this page: 'SAO PAULO, July 27, 2016 /PRNewswire/ --'. Include city, full date, and any distributor tag required by the wire service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph (news summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An opening paragraph that states the core news (who, what, when, where, why/so what).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This release opens by announcing Aberje launches the third edition of BRpr in July and summarizes the newsletter's purpose. The lead should quickly tell readers the essential facts and why it matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body content with key details and highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting paragraphs that elaborate on the announcement with specifics, named contributors, notable items, and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The body mentions authors (Paulo Nassar), topics (crisis, Rio Olympic Games), highlighted campaigns (Votorantim Cimentos, Pirelli, Volvo), and partnerships (Syracuse University). Use this space to provide relevant names, quotations, examples, and context that substantiate the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate / About section
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard short organizational description that explains who the organization is, its mission, history, scope, and core activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This release includes an 'About Aberje' section with founding date, mission, pillars (Advocacy, Content, Education and Career), membership count, and international relationships. Keep boilerplate brief, factual, and reusable across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear media contact details including name, role, phone number, and email address for follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Tato Carbonaro, Public Affairs and International Relations, +55 11 5727-9090, [email protected]'. Always provide at least one named contact with phone and email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-to-action or links to further resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Links or instructions for readers to access the product / register / obtain more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This release gives a registration link to receive the BRpr newsletter and a related_links URL. Include URLs or sign-up instructions where appropriate so interested readers can take next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source / attribution line
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit source or attribution identifying the origin of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page shows 'SOURCE Aberje'. When using wire services, include the source/company name to clarify provenance for editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language / regional labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Indication of language variants or regional editions when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents language/region labels (e.g., 'USA - English', 'Latin America - español'). For multinational communications, indicate language and target region or provide localized versions.
